To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have synthesized a depsipeptide containing two different moieties, one with metal chelation and DNA intercalating properties, the other one with metal cheling and redox properties.
the cytostatic properties of the compounds studied are related to their ability to reach DNA and to generate free radicals.

the cytotoxicity and DNA binding of the depsipeptide 1, which contains a peptide metal-cheling moiety and the anilino-acridine 1, are due to its ability to reach and bind DNA and to the redox mechanism which involves interactions between the drug, metals and molecular O2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new depsipeptides with anti-tumor properties, based on a metal-chelating and DNA-binding peptide moiety.
the design and synthesis of peptide-based compounds which are able to interact with the DNA and to generate free radicals.
the synthesis, the biological activity and the DNA binding of new peptide-metal-chelating compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these compounds, which are not active in themselves, could be used in combination with other drugs in the therapy of cancer, in the same way as bleomycin is currently used.
the cytotoxicity of the compounds is related to the ability of the metal chelating moieties to bind copper and to generate active oxygen species.
the anti-tumour activity of the drugs is the result of their ability to bind DNA and to produce active radical species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA binding and the free radicals formation are two essential features for the anti-tumor activity.
the biological activity of the drugs is related to both their DNA affinity and their ability to generate free radicals.
, in the case of 1, the DNA affinity and the ability to chelate metals are both necessary for the cytostatic activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single molecule can be endowed with two properties which are usually present in different molecules, thus leading to a new class of anti-tumor agents.
the synthesis of depsipeptide drugs is a feasible and promising way for the development of new anti-tumor drugs.
the introduction of a peptide metal-chelaing moiety into the structure of a drug known to interact with DNA does not improve the biological properties of the drug.
